chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from some of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding

the clay of the rain: that there is no problem with it contacting the garment for three days, unless it is known that something has impurified it after the rain. So if it contacts the garment after three days (of rainfall), then wash it; and if the road was clean, do not wash it.

key_terms.الطَّرِيقُ نَظِيفٌ: The road is clean — meaning free from known impurities
key_terms.طِينُ الْمَطَرِ: Rain clay/mud — the runoff mud formed during or after rainfall
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: No problem/no harm — a standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.نَجَّسَهُ: Has rendered impure — from najasah, ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Is rainwater mud on clothing ritually impure according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes an important legal ruling from one of the Imams (referred to as Abu al-Hasan) regarding ritual purity (taharah) and rain mud. The ruling permits rainwater mud to contact clothing for up to three days without causing ritual impurity, because rain naturally purifies what it mixes with. The exception arises if one has definitive knowledge that an impure substance (najasah) contaminated the mud after the rain stopped, or if the contact occurs more than three days after the rainfall. This reflects a fundamental principle in Shia jurisprudence: the presumption of purity (istishab al-taharah) unless impurity is definitively established.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from one of our companions,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the clay of the rain, that there is no problem with it for three days if it hits the clothes, unless if one knows that something has impurified it after the rain. So if it is hit after three days (of rainfall), then wash it, and if the street was clean, do not wash it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about

soil which is found with rain water. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful up to three days unless it is found out to have become Najis (unclean) by something after rainfall. If such drops sprinkle after three days, then you must wash, but if the road is clean, then you do not need to wash.’”
